title: Israel’s Nuclear Posture: Intellectual Antecedents and Doctrinal Foundations
central_claims: Israel should move from deliberate nuclear ambiguity toward selective disclosure to enhance deterrence credibility, within a coherent doctrine centered on deterrence rather than nuclear war fighting.
The doctrine should account for adversary perceptions and rationality, hybrid threats and wider power competition; nuclear capability is presented as indispensable to Israeli survival.

source_manifest.title: Israel’s Nuclear Posture: Intellectual Antecedents and Doctrinal Foundations
source_manifest.finding: Normative strategic essay argues for selective disclosure and coherent deterrence doctrine; does not present a comparative empirical policy test.

source_manifest.title: Israel’s strategic interest in nuclear disarmament
source_manifest.finding: Ferrero argues that nuclear abolition and a regional nuclear-weapon-free zone serve Israeli security, with assurance from intelligence, defense and conventional capabilities. Notes cite target. This is a counterargument, not an empirical disproof or an endorsement.

source_manifest.title: Israel’s Conventional and Nuclear Deterrence
source_manifest.finding: Beres explicitly cites the 2017 essay and reapplies its disclosure, credibility, adversary-perception and doctrine framework to conventional escalation. Acknowledges little evidence nuclear weapons reliably deter conventional attacks. Same-author use, not independent validation.

source_manifest.title: Increasing focus on nuclear weapons amid heightened escalation risks—new SIPRI Yearbook out now
source_manifest.finding: SIPRI still describes Israel as not publicly acknowledging its nuclear weapons. It discusses modernization and heightened nuclear risks; does not attribute policy to this essay.
